title: Pin 19 may carry 0.55-0.77 A, but Molex rates it 0.3 A with all pins at 55 C and 0.8 A only at 25 C.
what: Molex's product specification gives two current figures for this Micro-HDMI receptacle: 0.3 A per contact, tested with all 19 contacts carrying current at 55 C ambient with an 85 C limit, and 0.8 A at 25 C with no other condition. On this board only pin 19 carries power, so neither test matches the real use; a single powered contact is usually allowed more than the all-19 figure, so the high case is unqualified rather than shown to exceed a rating. The expected 0.27 A is 90 % of 0.3 A, but the 0.55 A high case and the current-switch limit of 0.63-0.77 A are covered only by the 25 C figure, and the board sits in a closed enclosure with no fan. The files cannot settle this; a Molex answer for one contact at a warm ambient, or a measured pin-19 temperature under load, would.
where: HDMI Extension Board V37, J610-J617 pin 19 (PORT1_5V ... PORT8_5V), fed by U701-U708 TPS2553 with R711-R718 = 37.4 kOhm; returns on pins 4/7/10/13/16 and the four SH pads (DGND). The same contact at the other cable end: Frontend J3 pin 19 (VIN_5V), MPN 467651001.
evidence: Molex PS-46765-003 rev 9: sheet 1 sec. 4.2, 0.8 A at 25 C; sec. 4.3, operating -30 to +85 C; sheet 2 sec. 5.1 item 4, 0.3 A minimum, all 19 circuits powered, 55 C maximum ambient, '85 C maximum temperature change' (EIA-364-70A); no derating curve. Farnell copy of the 0467651001 datasheet: 0.8 A maximum per contact. exports/hdmi/pads.csv J610: pin 19 PORT1_5V, no other power pins; exports/frontend/pads.csv J3: pin 19 VIN_5V. power_estimate/START_HERE.md line 35: 0.15 / 0.27 / 0.55 A at the 5 V pin. TI SLVS841G eq. 1-3 at 37.4 kOhm: 637 / 696 / 764 mA (630-771 mA with 1 % resistor tolerance). Ratios: 0.27/0.30 = 90 %, 0.55/0.80 = 69 %, 0.771/0.80 = 96 %. Pin 19 alone carries 3.4x (0.55 A) or 6.6x (0.771 A) the per-contact heat of the 0.3 A test, so the hot-spot rise cannot be read from the specification. design_inputs/START_HERE.md line 44 lists '0.8 A connector pin' without the 25 C condition. enclosure_V3/START_HERE.md line 62: closed enclosure, no fan, nothing simulated or measured.
source: Molex PS-46765-003 rev 9 (EC S2011-0455, 2010-11-19), sheets 1-2, secs. 4.2, 4.3 and 5.1 item 4, read from the distributor copy https://static.chipdip.ru/lib/026/DOC027026286.pdf because https://www.molex.com/en-us/products/part-detail/0467651001 timed out; Molex 0467651001 datasheet, Farnell copy (https://www.farnell.com/datasheets/1631775.pdf); TI TPS2553 data sheet SLVS841G, eq. 1-3.
consequence: In expected use nothing happens. Under the high load, or with a port held at its current limit, pin 19 at both cable ends may run hotter than Molex has qualified, risking contact wear or heat damage over time; the 0.8 A ceiling recorded in design_inputs is a 25 C figure, so the margin is smaller than recorded.
suggested_action: Ask Molex what continuous current one contact (pin 19, returns on pins 4/7/10/13/16 and shell) may carry at 50 C ambient for a 30 K rise, and whether PS-46765-003-001 changes the ratings. At bring-up, load one port at 0.55 A and then at the switch limit for 30 min inside the enclosure, and measure pin-19 and shell temperature at J61x and at Frontend J3.

title: The port current limit is only 80 mA above the high-case Frontend load; a cable loop near 1 ohm uses it up.
what: Each port switch (TPS2553) starts limiting at 630 mA at the earliest, set by a 37.4k resistor on its ILIM pin. The recorded high-case Frontend load is 0.55 A, so the margin at the board is about 80 mA. The Frontend's only 5 V load is a buck converter that draws constant power, so as resistance in the single cable +5 V wire (pin 19) lowers the far-end voltage, the port current rises; with a pin-19 loop of about 0.9-1.0 ohm the high case reaches the limit. The stimulation converter on the LDO board (LT3582-12) is not in the budget and adds at most about 0.07-0.08 A at 5 V, part of which the budget's 3.3 V reserve already covers.
where: HDMI Extension Board V37: U701-U708 (TPS2553DBVR) pin 5 ILIM with R711-R718 (37.4k); PORT1_5V-PORT8_5V from U70x pin 6 to J610-J617 pin 19; FE_5V = 5.02 V set by R700 40.2k / R701 10k. Frontend: J3.19 VIN_5V feeds only U16 (MPM3833C). FPGA-LDO A: U1 LT3582EUD-12 pin 5 on /VIN_3V3 (J2.68-70), feeding U9 LT3042 (/ASIC_VDD10) and U10 LT3094 (/ASIC_VSS10).
evidence: TI equations 1-3 (SLVS841G p.16-17) for 37.4k with 1% tolerance: 630 / 696 / 771 mA min / nom / max, matching Table 9-2 p.21; 36.5k gives 646-789 mA, 35.7k 661-805 mA, 42.2k 558-688 mA. inputs/hdmi/power_estimate/START_HERE.md section 1: 0.27 A expected and 0.55 A high case at 5 V including cable; VIN_3V3 row 0.30 A high against 0.13 A expected; section 4 excludes the stimulation rails. Constant-power solve (5.02 V source, 0.135 ohm max switch rDS(on) p.6 plus 0.034 ohm board copper): 2.75 W draws 0.595 A at a 0.5 ohm cable loop, 0.633 A at 0.9 ohm, 0.645 A at 1.0 ohm, and collapses to 3.09 V at 2.0 ohm; the expected 1.35 W draws 0.29-0.31 A even at 1-2 ohm. Stimulation upper bound: 1024 stimulators x 22.5 uA = 23 mA from a 12 V rail = 0.28 W, or +0.072-0.082 A at 5 V after the LT3582 and U16; 3.14 W (stimulation added in full) draws 0.689 A at 0.5 ohm. The 771 mA maximum is below the 0.8 A per-contact rating of the Molex 46765-1001 (distributor copies of the Molex sheet; molex.com not read). No cable length or gauge is recorded in inputs/.
source: TI TPS2553 datasheet SLVS841G, equations 1-3 p.16-17, Table 9-2 p.21, rDS(on) p.6, current-limit thermal cycling section 9.1.1 p.18, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps2553.pdf; Molex 46765-1001 0.8 A per contact (distributor copies); ASIC reference rows B14-B20 (128 stimulators, 22.5 uA, under 200 Hz).
consequence: With the high-case load on a thin or long cable, the port goes into current limit, VIN_5V sags, U16 drops out and the Frontend and ASICs brown out or hiccup. The connector is not overrun: the limit stays under 0.8 A and in a hard short the switch thermal-cycles.
suggested_action: Measure the 5 V current of one full stack (start-up, recording, full stimulation) and the pin-19 loop resistance of the chosen cable; if the loop is above about 0.5-0.7 ohm, use shorter or heavier cables or the BOM-only change R700 = 42.2k (5.22 V).
verification: Upheld after a third independent check

title: U700's output capacitors C704-C707 are X5R parts rated only to 85 C, not the X7R/X6S/X7S types TI lists, and two sit 1.3 mm from the hot module.
what: TI's recommended output capacitors for the TPSM63606 are all X7R, X6S, X7S or X6T, rated to 105-125 C. The BOM number C77101 picks Murata GRM32ER61C476KE15L, an X5R part rated -55 to +85 C; the schematic gives only '47uF', with no MPN or dielectric. C704 and C705 sit 1.27 mm from U700's pads on its VOUT/PGND copper. At the high-case load in 40-50 C air, U700 is estimated near 90-100 C (HDMI-03, HDMI-19), so these capacitors can reach their limit. Capacitance is fine: about -30 % at 5 V leaves about 30 uF each, against TI's 30 uF total minimum.
evidence: V37 BOM line '47uF,C704-C707,C_1210_3225Metric,C77101'. exports/hdmi/parts.csv: JLCPCB C77101, MPN empty. JLC/LCSC C77101 = GRM32ER61C476KE15L, 47 uF 16 V X5R. Murata sheet p.1: operating range -55 to 85 C; p.2: DC bias about -30 % at 5 V. TI SLVSGB4B Table 8-3 lists only X7R/X6S/X6T/X7S; Table 8-1 gives a 30 uF effective minimum at 5 V. board.json: C704/C705 are 1.27 mm and C706/C707 4.67 mm from U700's pads. In stock at JLC today: C84494 GRM32ER71A476KE15L (X7R 10 V) 11,718; C415541 GRM32ER71A476ME15L (TI-listed) 675.
source: TI TPSM63606 data sheet SLVSGB4B (Apr 2022), section 8.3.4, Tables 8-1 and 8-3, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tpsm63606.pdf. Murata GRM32ER61C476KE15 data sheet (2013-09-23), RS distributor copy https://docs.rs-online.com/7185/0900766b813d2ca9.pdf, pp.1-2. https://jlcpcb.com/partdetail/C77101, https://jlcpcb.com/partdetail/C84494, https://jlcpcb.com/partdetail/C415541.
consequence: Above 85 C the X5R parts age faster and run outside the maker's rating. Failure would be gradual, because the minimum capacitance is still met.
suggested_action: BOM-only change: fit C704-C707 with TI's X7R GRM32ER71A476KE15L/ME15L (C84494/C415541) or a 47 uF 16 V X6S 1210 on the same pads. Log their temperature next to U700 at bring-up.

title: One U700 feedback fault can drive FE_5V to about 11.9 V, past the 7 V port switches and the heads' 6.5 V input limit, and nothing on FE_5V clamps it.
what: U700 sets FE_5V only through R700/R701 on its FB pin. Its power-good output, which enables all eight ports, also measures FE_5V through FB, so the module has no overvoltage check that works without FB. An open R700, a grounded FB pin or a shorted high-side switch drives FE_5V to about 11.7-12 V; power-good then keeps the ports off or turns them off, but the eight TPS2553 switches (7 V maximum) are left holding that voltage, and a fault that appears while running reaches every head for about 1-3 ms before the switches open. A wrong divider value (R700 about 55-115 kOhm or R701 about 3.5-7.3 kOhm) is worse: U700 regulates normally, power-good stays high, and every head receives a steady 6.5-11.9 V against its 6.5 V input maximum.
where: HDMI Extension Board V37. U700 TPSM63606: pin 10 FB (Net-(U700-FB): R700 40.2 kOhm to FE_5V at 129.4/60.9; R701 10 kOhm to DGND at 128.8/62.4; C708 22 pF), pin 11 AGND, pin 13 PG, pin 14 EN/SYNC on +VDCIN. Net FE_5V: 35 pads, TP700 at 134.25/65.5. PORT_ENABLE: R703 10 kOhm to FE_5V, U701-U708 pin 3. U701-U708 TPS2553: pin 1 IN; pin 4 FAULT, fed from FE_5V through R721-R728 3.3 kOhm and D701-D708. PORT1_5V-PORT8_5V run to J610-J617 pin 19. At each head, Frontend J3.19 VIN_5V feeds C206/C207 (22 uF 10 V), C209, and U16 MPM3833C pins 4, 13 and 14.
evidence: Circuit (exports/hdmi/netlist.xml, pads.csv, parts.csv): - Net-(U700-FB) has 4 nodes: U700.10, R700.1, R701.2, C708.2. - FE_5V has 35 pads; none is a TVS, Zener, fuse or crowbar. - Each PORTn_5V has 4 nodes. - PORT_ENABLE = U700.13, R703.1, U701-U708.3. - U700 pins 10/11 (FB/AGND) and pins 13/14 (PG/EN on +VDCIN) are 0.25 mm apart. - Frontend VIN_5V = J3.19, C206, C207, C209, TP14, U16.4/13/14 (exports/frontend/netlist.xml). End value: with FB open or grounded, U700 runs at maximum duty. tON(max) is 9 us and tOFF(min) 85 ns, giving 99.1 % duty, so FE_5V is about 11.9 V at 12.0 V input, or 11.7-11.8 V with the ports loaded. (a) Fault present at power-up: - FB stays below the 94 % PG threshold, so PG never rises and the ports stay off. - FE_5V reaches about 11.9 V roughly 0.2 ms after switching starts (8.3 A into 53-125 uF). - It stays there with or without hiccup, because only about 1 mA loads it. - Each TPS2553 then holds IN about 11.9 V, IN-OUT about 11.9 V and FAULT about 10 V (FE_5V through R72x, minus the LED drop at microamp leakage). That is 1.4-1.7x its 7 V maximum, for as long as 12 V is applied. - If one switch fails short, its head gets about 11.6-11.9 V: 1.8x U16's 6.5 V maximum and 1.2x the 10 V rating of C206/C207. Wrong ratio: FE_5V = 1.0 V x (1 + R700/R701), and PG judges FB. In every case below PG reads good, the ports are on, and the EN pins sit at FE_5V through R703. - R700 56.2k: 6.62 V. - R700 75k: 8.50 V. - R700 100k: 11.0 V. - R700 110k: 11.89 V (FB 0.991 V). - R701 6.8k: 6.91 V. - R701 4.99k: 9.06 V. - R701 3.9k: 11.31 V. From R700 about 120k, or R701 about 3.3k, the output saturates, PG goes low and case (a) applies. (b) Fault appearing with the ports on: - PG falls 120 us later. Each TPS2553 keeps conducting about 1 ms after EN falls (Figure 6-2), and toff can be up to 3 ms. - C_total at 5 V is 272-484 uF: 125 uF on the board plus 8 x (C72x + C206/C207 + C209). - Source current is 7.4-10.3 A; load is 2.2-5.0 A. FE_5V therefore rises at 5-30 V/ms. - 24-corner model: FE_5V is 5.6-10.3 V when PG falls, crosses 6.5 V after 44-290 us, and reaches 11.1-11.8 V by the typical switch opening. - If U700 follows the LM61460 hiccup rule (128 cycles below 40 %, not in dropout), it stops at 190-310 us with FE_5V at 6.7-11.3 V. FE_5V stays as low as 5.9-6.0 V only if the head capacitors lose no capacitance with DC bias. In 5 of the 24 corners U700 reaches dropout first, giving 11.4-11.9 V. - After that, FE_5V sits at about 11.9 V behind the open switches. High-side short: FE_5V follows +VDCIN to about 12 V through the 2.2 uH inductor within about 0.1 ms (overshoot not modelled). PG trips on overvoltage after 120 us, so the heads see about 12 V for 1-3 ms. The switches then hold 12 V. Pin 13-14 bridge: puts 12 V on all eight EN pins, and PG can no longer turn the ports off. TI does not specify how the TPS2553 behaves or fails above 7 V. Unknown links in the damage chain: (1) Whether each TPS2553 survives 10-12 V, and if not, whether it fails open or short. (2) How fast U700 reacts to an FB step, and when it hiccups. SLVSGB4B does not say. (3) Whether U16 fails open, or fails with a high-side short that passes about 12 V to VIN_3V3. (4) Ratings and failure modes of the VIN_3V3 loads: Frontend U2-U4/U13 MPM3833C, U5/U6 TPS74801 BIAS, U10-U12; FPGA-LDO U1 LT3582-12, three LT3042, four TPS7A2015. Not re-read. (5) ASIC supply maximums (unknown, SYS-45). Model scripts: a review working file (not published) and hiccup_race.py.
source: TI TPSM63606 SLVSGB4B (Oct 2021, rev. Apr 2022), https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tpsm63606.pdf: - Table 6-1 p.3-4 (FB: do not leave open or connect to ground; VLDOIN). - 7.1 p.5 (VOUT/FB 16 V; VLDOIN min(VIN+0.3, 16) V). - 7.5 p.7-8: VFB 1.0 V; IL_HS 8.3/9.3/10.3 A; IL_LS 6.5/7.1/7.7 A; VHICCUP 40 %; tW 80 ms; PGUV 92/94/96.5 %; PGOV 105/107/110 %; IOV 0.5 mA; tPG_FLT_FALL 120 us; tPG_FLT_RISE 1.5-2.5 ms; tON(max) 9 us; tOFF(min) 65/85 ns. - 8.2 block diagram p.14 (2.2 uH). - 8.3.9 p.19 (PG judged at FB). - 8.3.11 p.20; 8.3.12 p.21. TI LM61460 SNVSBD5D (rev. Jul 2022), https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/lm61460.pdf: 8.3.10 p.17-19, 8.3.12 p.20-21 (hiccup after 128 consecutive cycles below 0.4x the set point, not in dropout), 8.4.3.5 p.26. This is a related controller, used only for the hiccup rule that the module sheet does not spell out. TI TPS2553 SLVS841G (rev. Oct 2026), https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps2553.pdf: 6.1 p.5 (IN/OUT/EN/ILIM/FAULT -0.3 to 7 V; IN-OUT +/-7 V), 6.3 p.5 (VIN 2.5-6.5 V), 6.5 p.6 (toff 3 ms max), Figure 6-2 p.8. MPS MPM3833C Rev. 1.0 (12/3/2018), p.3 (all pins except SW -0.3 to +6.5 V; VIN 2.75-6 V), https://www.monolithicpower.com/en/documentview/productdocument/index/version/2/document_type/Datasheet/lang/en/sku/MPM3833CGRH-Z/document_id/4426/ (linked from https://www.monolithicpower.com/en/mpm3833c.html). Murata GRM32ER61C476KE15 product sheet (updated 2013/09/23), p.2 DC-bias chart. Copy at a review working file (not published); product page https://www.murata.com/en-us/products/productdetail?partno=GRM32ER61C476KE15L. The GRM21BR61A226ME44L curve was not read (40-100 % assumed). LCSC C308258: https://www.lcsc.com/product-detail/C308258.html. Project files: - inputs/hdmi/V37_order/HDMI_Extension_Board_V37_BOM.csv - inputs/hdmi/V36_prefab_fixes/START_HERE.md (R700 42.2 kOhm option) - inputs/hdmi/V35_prefab_review/ALL_FINDINGS.md (TP700 half under the XEM8310) LED forward voltage at microamp leakage: engineering judgement; the Lite-On LTST-C190KRKT sheet was not read.
consequence: One 0603 resistor, one QFN solder bridge or one module failure can overstress all eight port switches at once, or damage up to eight head stacks together: U16 first, then possibly everything on VIN_3V3 and the ASIC rails. The wrong-value case passes power-good and gives no warning. The V36/V37 records already plan to rework this exact resistor (the R700 40.2 to 42.2 kOhm option), which raises the chance of a wrong value.
suggested_action: Write a first-power rule into the HDMI bring-up notes: - Power J4 with no HDMI cables. Probe C704-C707 pin 1 if the XEM8310 is fitted. - Confirm TP700 reads 4.9-5.15 V, TP701-TP708 read the same as TP700, and PORT_ENABLE at R703 pin 1 is near 5 V, not 12 V. - Stop if any reading is outside this. - Repeat after any rework of U700, R700/R701 (including the 42.2 kOhm option) or a port switch. For the next revision, add an overvoltage cut-off on FE_5V that senses FE_5V directly and is rated for the 12-15 V input. Options: an eFuse rated 16 V or more ahead of the port switches, port switches rated 16 V or more with their own OV cut-off, or a crowbar that U700's current limit and hiccup then hold. A TVS alone cannot absorb U700's 8-10 A.

title: U602 drives the FT232H TDO pin while the FT232H, in its default UART mode, also drives that pin.
what: The level shifter U602 (TXU0304) drives HOST_TDO from a push-pull output straight into FT232H pin 15 (ADBUS2), with no series resistor. U602 is enabled whenever a powered target is selected, and when the target's TDO is idle and floating, U602's weak input pull-down makes that output drive low. In its default asynchronous UART mode the FT232H uses ADBUS2 as the RTS# output, so two outputs fight until software switches the chip to MPSSE, its JTAG engine. The board fits a blank EEPROM; that a blank EEPROM leaves the chip in UART mode rests on secondary sources, so FTDI's own documents or a vendor answer should confirm it.
where: HDMI Extension Board V37: U602 pin 5 (A4Y) on net HOST_TDO to U501 pin 15 (ADBUS2); R509 10k pull-up to FTDI3V3 is the only other part on the net; U602 pin 8 OE = DRIVE_ENABLE from U605 (TPS3808) pin 1, gated by the VREF window and the MASTER switch SW601; U505 93LC56BT-I/SN EEPROM.
evidence: exports/hdmi/netlist.xml: HOST_TDO = U501.15, U602.5 (tri_state output), R509.1; R509.2 = FTDI3V3; U602.8 = DRIVE_ENABLE = U605.1, R615, R616; U605.3 MR_N = WINDOW_GATE (U603, R614 to SW601.6). JTAG_TDO_1V8 = U602.10 plus COM5 of U610-U618 only, with no pull resistor; the Frontend's FPGA_JTAG_TDO = U1.T8 and J3.18 only. TI SCES935A: weak pull-downs on all inputs (p.6 note 3), 5 Mohm typical (section 9.3.1.1); push-pull outputs (section 9.3.3); absolute maximum continuous output current +/-25 mA. FT232H datasheet FT_000288 v1.81 p.11 (third-party copy; ftdichip.com returned 403): ADBUS2 is an output whose default function is RTS#. The Linux ftdi_sio driver assumes an erased EEPROM gives async UART mode. The original review notes the Opal Kelly BRK8305 A03 has the same always-on TDO buffer but ships a pre-configured EEPROM; this comparison was not re-checked.
source: TI TXU0304 datasheet SCES935A (Nov 2021), p.6, sections 9.3.1.1 and 9.3.3, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/txu0304.pdf; FTDI FT232H datasheet FT_000288 v1.81 p.11 (third-party copy, FTDI site not readable).
consequence: From first bring-up until the EEPROM sets a non-UART mode, and whenever the chip sits in UART mode with a target selected, both drivers short into each other. This stresses U602 and U501 beyond their datasheet limits, though it is not an immediate failure.
suggested_action: Confirm the ADBUS2 state with a blank EEPROM and after programming from FTDI's own datasheet or FTDI; if it is driven, add a 330 ohm to 1 kohm series resistor between U602.5 and U501.15, or keep SW601 OFF until the EEPROM is programmed.

title: Through a 2 m cable, Frontend JTAG works only up to about 5.5 MHz TCK, well below the common 15 MHz default.
what: In JTAG the target's TDO answer must get back to the FT232H within half a TCK clock period. The round trip adds the U602 level-shifter delay both ways, the cable both ways, the FPGA's clock-to-TDO time, a heavily loaded 225 mm TDO trunk, and the FT232H's input setup time. In the worst case with a 2 m cable that is about 91 ns, which limits TCK to about 5.5 MHz (about 6.2 MHz with a 1 m cable). Vivado's default for Digilent-type cables is 15 MHz; whether an FT232H programmed for this board gets that default was not confirmed.
where: HDMI Extension Board V37: JTAG_TCK_1V8 (R601 22R) and JTAG_TDO_1V8 trunks from U602 to U610-U618; per-port 100R (R640-R671, e.g. R643 on HDMI1_JTAG_TDO); J610-J617 pins 17/18; cable; Frontend U1 F8/T8.
evidence: Loop at 2 m: U602 A to B 19 ns + TCK trunk about 4 ns + cable 10 ns + Artix-7 TCK to TDO 7 ns + cable 10 ns + TDO trunk RC about 16 ns to 50% + U602 B to A 14 ns + FT232H TDO setup 11 ns = about 91 ns; 1/(2 x 91 ns) = about 5.5 MHz. TXU0304 SCES935A section 7.11 p.14 (VCCA 3.3 V, VCCB 1.8 V): A to B 19 ns max, B to A 14 ns max (-40 to 85 C). exports/hdmi/nets.csv: trunk copper TDO 224.88 mm, TDI 225.92, TCK 232.71, TMS 226.67 mm, 0.15 mm on L3/L6. Trunk capacitance 8 x 8.5 pF (COM OFF) + 21.5 pF (ON) + about 20-25 pF trace + 4 pF = about 115-120 pF (TS3A27518E SCDS260F section 6.5 p.7; ron 6.2 ohm max). AMD DS181 v1.27.1: TTCKTDO 7.00 ns max. FTDI FT_000288 v1.82 Table 4.4 p.37: TDI setup 11 ns min. Cable about 5 ns/m (engineering judgement). UG908: 15 MHz default for Digilent cables, 6 MHz for the USB cable.
source: TI TXU0304 SCES935A section 7.11; TI TS3A27518E SCDS260F section 6.5; AMD DS181 v1.27.1 boundary-scan switching table; FTDI FT_000288 v1.82 Table 4.4; AMD UG908 'Reconnecting to a Target Device with a Lower JTAG Clock Frequency'; engineering judgement for cable delay.
consequence: At a 15 MHz TCK, scans or programming of a Frontend may fail intermittently or read wrong IDCODEs, which looks like a cable or board fault.
suggested_action: At bring-up, set the hw_server TCK to 3-6 MHz for Frontend targets and step it up while checking IDCODE reads; record the working limit per cable length.

title: Y500's load mismatch puts the FT232H clock about 20-55 ppm fast, outside the FT232H's own +/-30 ppm input limit.
what: FTDI's datasheet asks for a 12 MHz input within +/-30 ppm. Y500 is cut for an 18 pF load, but two 18 pF capacitors plus pin and trace capacitance give it about 11-14 pF. That pulls it fast by roughly 20-55 ppm, before its own +/-10 ppm tolerance and +/-10 ppm drift (-20 to 70 C). HDMI-22 compared this only with the USB +/-500 ppm limit; against FTDI's limit it is most likely out of specification. USB will probably still work, as on Opal Kelly's BRK8305 with the same values.
where: HDMI Extension Board V37: Y500 SJK 7U12000E18UCG (C524717) on U501 OSCI/OSCO; C503/C504 KEMET C0402C180J5GACTU, 18 pF.
evidence: FT_000288 v1.82, section 6.3, p.55: '12MHz +/- 0.003% crystal' and Table 6.1, Fin 12 MHz +/-30 ppm. SJK spec A1 (2017-05-10): CL 18 pF, C0 3 pF max, +/-10 ppm at 25 C, +/-10 ppm over -20..70 C, aging +/-3 ppm/yr, no C1. Pulling dF/F = C1/2 x [1/(C0+CLeff) - 1/(C0+18 pF)]. With C1 3-6 fF (assumed), C0 1.5-3 pF and CLeff 11-14 pF this gives +19 to +57 ppm; for example C1 4 fF, C0 2 pF, CLeff 12.5 pF gives +38 ppm. With 27 pF capacitors CLeff is about 16-18 pF and the offset is about 0-10 ppm. JLC's own C524717 listing gives +/-10 ppm and +/-30 ppm, -40 to 85 C (a review working file (not published)), the +/-30 ppm stability HDMI-22 used; if that applies, the total error is larger still.
source: FTDI DS_FT232H FT_000288 v1.82, section 6.3, Table 6.1, p.55, https://ftdichip.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/DS_FT232H.pdf (read from a copy fetched by an earlier reviewer; ftdichip.com returned 403 today). SJK 7U12000E18UCG spec A1, LCSC copy https://datasheet.lcsc.com/datasheet/pdf/5264ef3486a068e24cbf9f4599b78983.pdf?productCode=C524717. JLCPCB part page https://jlcpcb.com/partdetail/C524717 (listing data in a review working file (not published)). Crystal pulling formula from memory, not re-read.
consequence: The FT232H runs outside its stated clock tolerance and USB has less margin than the datasheet intends. Enumeration will most likely still work.
suggested_action: BOM-only change of C503/C504 to 27 pF C0G 0402, FTDI's example value, on the same pads. Alternatively, record a decision to accept 18 pF.

title: U602 has no bypass capacitor closer than about 9.5 mm to either supply pin.
what: U602 is a TXU0304 level shifter that moves the JTAG signals between 3.3 V and 1.8 V. A bypass capacitor is a small capacitor placed right at a chip's supply pin to supply the short current pulses drawn when its outputs switch. TI asks for one on each supply pin, as close to the device as possible, but the nearest capacitors here are 9.5 to 10.4 mm away and the 1.8 V supply has no plane, only 0.2-0.3 mm track. The capacitors sit where they were in V35, so V36 and V37 did not move them.
where: HDMI Extension Board V37, bottom side (layer 6). U602 (TXU0304PWR at 146.0, 75.75): pin 1 FTDI3V3 at (143.14, 77.70), pin 14 +1.8V at (148.86, 77.70). Nearest capacitors C603 (2.2 uF), C604 and C605 (100 nF, 0603, bottom).
evidence: exports/hdmi/pads.csv: straight-line distance from U602.1 to C604.1 (152.25, 72.775) is 10.36 mm; from U602.14 to C603.1 (152.25, 68.775) 9.55 mm and to C605.1 (141.87, 71.14) 9.59 mm. No other FTDI3V3 capacitor is within 23 mm. Routed paths are 13.6 mm (pin 1 to C604) and 10.3-10.8 mm (pin 14 to C603/C605); inputs/hdmi/V35_prefab_review/ALL_FINDINGS.md line 633 gives the same pad coordinates. exports/hdmi/nets.csv: +1.8V is L1/L3/L6 track of 0.2-0.3 mm with no zone; FTDI3V3 is track only.
source: TI TXU0304 datasheet SCES935A, section 12.1 Layout Guidelines, p.25 (0.1 uF bypass, 1 uF in parallel optional, as close to the device as possible), https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/txu0304.pdf
consequence: Supply bounce when the outputs switch can add noise or false edges on the JTAG lines, including TCK. The risk is low at JTAG speeds.
suggested_action: At the next layout touch, move C604/C605 or add 100 nF capacitors right beside U602 pins 1 and 14.

title: The U801-U816 ESD pads do not follow TI's DQA0010A pattern: signal pads are wider and ground pads narrower.
what: U801-U816 are TPD4E02B04 ESD protection arrays in a 1.0 x 2.5 mm, 10-pad USON package with 0.5 mm pitch. The land pattern (the copper pads the part is soldered to) makes all ten pads 0.30 x 0.55 mm with row centres 0.77 mm apart, while TI's example uses 0.20 mm signal pads, 0.40 mm ground pads (pins 3 and 8), 0.565 mm pad length and 0.835 mm row centres. The copper gap between adjacent signal pads is 0.20 mm instead of TI's 0.30 mm, but the paste openings put about the same solder on the signal pads as TI's stencil, so the chance of a solder bridge rises only modestly. The ground pads get about half the paste TI shows.
where: HDMI Extension Board V37, U801-U816 (16 parts, footprint Shared_JTAG_V9:USON-10_2.5x1.0mm_P0.5mm), near the left edge at about x 75 mm.
evidence: boards/hdmi/libraries/Shared_JTAG_V9.pretty/USON-10_2.5x1.0mm_P0.5mm.kicad_mod and all 16 instances in HDMI_Extension_Board_V37.kicad_pcb: pads 0.30 x 0.55 mm, centres x = +/-0.385, pitch 0.5 mm, pads 3/8 the same size; solder_paste_margin -0.04 gives 0.22 x 0.47 mm apertures. Signal paste 0.103 mm2 against TI's 0.20 x 0.565 = 0.113 mm2; ground paste about 0.10 mm2 against TI's about 0.20 mm2. Board setup pad_to_mask_clearance 0 and solder_mask_min_width 0.1 leave a 0.20 mm mask web between pads. TI's own pattern has 0.30 mm gaps between signal pads and 0.20 mm beside pads 3/8. inputs/hdmi/V37_order/ORDER_NOTE_FOR_JLC_V37.md item 7: 0.22 x 0.47 mm apertures, 0.10 mm stencil.
source: TI TPD4E02B04 datasheet SLVSD85B (Jul 2016), p.24 example board layout and p.25 example stencil, package DQA0010A, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tpd4e02b04.pdf
consequence: A bridge would short a cable signal line (MGT RX, clock, command or SYNC) to its neighbour or to ground and is hard to see under the part; the smaller ground paste gives a weaker ground joint. The added risk over TI's pattern is modest.
suggested_action: Ask JLC at file review to confirm the pads and paste are acceptable, or at the next layout touch narrow the signal pads to 0.20-0.25 mm and widen pads 3/8 to 0.40 mm.

title: L3 is about 9.5 % copper against about 93 % on L2 and L4, and no balancing or bow/twist limit is decided.
what: A multilayer board stays flattest when each layer's copper is matched by similar copper on its mirror layer about the board centre. L3 (In2.Cu) has no pour and is about 9.5 % copper, while L2, L4 and L5 are about 93 %, so L3 is unbalanced against L2 in its own core and against its mirror L4 across the centre prepreg; L1/L6 and L2/L5 are balanced. Uneven copper can make a board bow or twist during lamination and reflow, but the thin 0.5 oz inner copper and this common layer arrangement limit the effect, and the files cannot predict how much bow results. The order note invites JLC to propose balancing copper but sets no bow/twist limit, and no decision is recorded.
where: HDMI Extension Board V37, L3 (In2.Cu) against L2 (In1.Cu) and L4 (In3.Cu), whole board. Most sensitive: the J6 card-edge tongue (y 149-162) and the XEM8310 connectors MC1/MC2/MC3 (x 147-192, y 67-133).
evidence: Per-layer copper union (tracks, flashed pads, vias, fills) from boards/hdmi/HDMI_Extension_Board_V37.kicad_pcb (a review working file (not published), cu3.py): L1 12.9 %, L2 93.6 %, L3 9.5 % (1696 of 17820 mm2; tracks 1242 mm2, 991 via pads 109 mm2, plus 172 through-hole pads), L4 92.9 %, L5 93.0 %, L6 14.4 %. exports/hdmi/zones.csv: no L3 zones. exports/hdmi/stackup.txt: 0.30 mm core L2-L3, 2x7628 prepreg L3-L4, 0.30 mm core L4-L5, inner copper 0.0152 mm. inputs/hdmi/V37_order/ORDER_NOTE_FOR_JLC_V37.md PCB item 2: 13/9/14 % against about 93 %, no thieving within 1.0 mm of pairs, 'please propose it', no bow/twist limit.
source: Engineering judgement (balanced copper about the board mid-plane). The IPC-6012 bow/twist limit of 0.75 % for SMT boards was not checked (paid standard).
consequence: If nothing is added, the board may bow more than expected, and a bowed card can seat poorly in the PCIe slot or strain the XEM8310 connector joints. How likely this is cannot be predicted from the files.
suggested_action: Decide before ordering: add a hatched DGND fill on L3 kept 1.0 mm from every pair, or tell JLC in writing that L3 thieving outside the 1.0 mm keep-out is wanted. In both cases ask JLC to state the bow/twist limit they will hold.

title: JLC's +/-10 % thickness tolerance allows a 1.76 mm board, above the note's 1.70 mm limit at the fingers.
what: The order note says board thickness at the PCIe gold fingers must stay within 1.44-1.70 mm (PCIe 1.57 +/- 0.13 mm, as given in the note). JLC's published tolerance for boards of 1.0 mm or more is +/-10 % of the ordered thickness, which for the ordered 1.6 mm allows 1.44-1.76 mm. So a board can be within JLC's tolerance yet up to 0.06 mm thicker than the note's upper limit. Unless JLC confirms the narrower window, only a caliper measurement of the tongue settles it.
where: HDMI Extension Board V37, J6 card edge (tongue y 151.1-162.05); ORDER_NOTE_FOR_JLC_V37.md, Gold fingers section, last bullet.
evidence: Order note: 1.44-1.70 mm at the fingers. Stack-up JLC06161H-2116, ordered as 1.6 mm. Laminate sum 2 x 0.035 + 4 x 0.0152 + 2 x (0.127 + 0.0964) + 2 x 0.3 + 2 x 0.2084 = 1.5944 mm, plus 0.02 mm of mask (boards/hdmi/HDMI_Extension_Board_V37.kicad_pcb thickness 1.5944; exports/hdmi/stackup.txt). JLC: +/-10 % for 1.0 mm or more, so 1.6 mm x 0.9 to 1.6 mm x 1.1 = 1.44-1.76 mm.
source: JLCPCB PCB capabilities, board thickness tolerance (https://jlcpcb.com/capabilities/pcb-capabilities) and JLCPCB 6-layer PCB page (https://jlcpcb.com/6-layer-pcb), both read 11 Nov 2026. The PCIe CEM value 1.57 +/- 0.13 mm is taken from the order note, not re-read; the CEM document is not public.
consequence: A board above 1.70 mm at the fingers may not enter the slot or may over-stress the slot contacts. Without a confirmed window, fit is known only by measuring each board.
suggested_action: Ask JLC to confirm 1.44-1.70 mm at the fingers before production, and measure the tongue with calipers on receipt before first insertion.

title: The PCIe fingers will be thin, soft ENIG immersion gold, not the hard gold card-edge contacts normally use.
what: JLC makes gold fingers only with ENIG (electroless nickel, immersion gold): a gold layer about 0.025-0.05 um thick over 3-6 um of nickel, deposited chemically rather than electroplated. Card-edge contacts in PCIe practice normally use hard (electroplated) gold, which wears much more slowly. JLC's 6-layer page lists the finish as 2 uin ENIG, so the thicker option appears to be the standard choice for this board; the order note says only 'ENIG' and does not confirm it.
where: HDMI Extension Board V37, J6 fingers A1-A49 and B1-B49; ORDER_NOTE_FOR_JLC_V37.md, Gold fingers bullet 1; stack-up copper_finish "ENIG".
evidence: jlcpcb.com/help/article/jlcpcb-gold-fingers: gold fingers only when ENIG is chosen; no hard gold or thickness given. jlcpcb.com/help/article/jlcpcb-surface-finish: gold 1 or 2 uin (about 0.025-0.05 um), nickel about 3-6 um. jlcpcb.com/6-layer-pcb: surface finish 'ENIG 2u"'. A JLC blog post (seen only as a search result; the page returned 404) says 6-20 layer boards default to 2 uin at no extra cost. exports/hdmi/stackup.txt copper_finish "ENIG"; the order note gives 6 layers and 'ENIG'.
source: JLCPCB help pages: gold fingers (https://jlcpcb.com/help/article/jlcpcb-gold-fingers) and surface finish (https://jlcpcb.com/help/article/jlcpcb-surface-finish); JLCPCB 6-layer PCB page (https://jlcpcb.com/6-layer-pcb); all read 11 Nov 2026. The PCIe CEM contact plating requirement was not read (document not public); the hard-gold expectation is engineering judgement.
consequence: The fingers wear after repeated insertions, and contact resistance can rise over time. This is acceptable for a lab card inserted a few times.
suggested_action: Confirm 2 uin ENIG on the JLC order page, and record an insertion-count limit for the card.

title: 210 vias have 0.15 mm drills (10.6:1), and 64 sit exactly at JLC's 0.20 mm inner hole-to-copper minimum.
what: 210 of the board's 991 vias use 0.15 mm drills in a 1.594 mm board, an aspect ratio (board thickness divided by hole diameter) of 10.6:1. 64 of them have the hole edge 0.2005 mm from other-net copper (the DGND pour) on inner layers L2, L4 and L5. Both values meet JLC's published minimums and the capability page gives no aspect-ratio limit, so this is zero margin, not a violation. The remaining risk is plating quality in thin, deep holes and no room for drill position error; the 6-8:1 aspect-ratio guide the order note cites should be checked before it is relied on.
where: HDMI Extension Board V37, 0.15/0.25 mm vias at J610-J617 (104), U801-U816 (40), U501 (3), C508 (1) and 62 others; inner layers L2/L4/L5 against the DGND pour, for example HDMI1_JTAG_TCK at (71.6, 143.9) and B64_L11P_GC at (70.38, 106.8).
evidence: Order Gerber ZIP, HDMI_Extension_Board_V37-PTH.drl: T1C0.150 210 hits, T2C0.200 722, T3C0.300 59, all vias, 991 in total. 1.5944 mm / 0.15 mm = 10.6:1. pcbnew measurement of hole edge to other-net copper (pours, tracks, pads, vias) on In1-In4: 0.15 mm vias minimum 0.2005 mm, with 64 distinct vias at that value on each of L2/L4/L5 (192 instances); 0.20 mm vias minimum 0.25 mm; 0.30 mm vias minimum 0.35 mm. JLC: multilayer via minimum 0.15 mm hole / 0.25 mm via; inner via hole to copper 0.2 mm.
source: JLCPCB PCB capabilities (https://jlcpcb.com/capabilities/pcb-capabilities) and JLCPCB 6-layer PCB page (https://jlcpcb.com/6-layer-pcb), read 11 Nov 2026: via minimum 0.15/0.25 mm, inner via hole to copper 0.2 mm, no aspect-ratio limit stated.
consequence: If plating in the thin holes is poor or a drill wanders, opens or near-shorts at the HDMI ports would be hard to find. If JLC flags the vias at file review, the order is held.
suggested_action: Keep the written-confirmation request for the 0.15 mm drill and the 0.20 mm inner clearance in the note and wait for JLC's answer before production; this is prudent, though JLC's published rules do not require it.

title: The Micro-HDMI mouths sit flush with the left edge, not 0.70 mm proud, and no left-edge tolerance is ordered.
what: Molex's recommended layout puts the board edge 1.70 mm in front of the front shell-slot centre, so the receptacle face stands 0.70 mm beyond the edge. On this board the edge is 2.404 mm in front of the slot centre, so the board runs 0.704 mm past Molex's edge line and the eight mouths are flush with the edge. The order note already places panel tabs only between shells and forbids any tab stub or burr proud of the left edge, but it asks for +/-0.1 mm routing only on the card-edge tongue, not the left edge. Whether a slightly proud edge stops a plug depends on the cable's overmold (the moulded plastic around the plug), which nothing in the files settles.
where: HDMI Extension Board V37, left Edge.Cuts at x 64.676 (y 47.95-157.55); J610-J617 front shell slots at x 67.08, rotation -90, top side; ORDER_NOTE_FOR_JLC_V37.md lines 55-59 and 69-71.
evidence: Molex SD-46765-001 rev D1 sheet 5: front slot 1.70 +/-0.05 mm from the PCB front edge, connector front interface 0.70 mm beyond the edge; sheet 2: 2.40 mm from front face to front tab centre, 3.36 mm between tabs; sheet 1: interface point 1.53 mm above the PCB. pcbnew on the V37 board: slots at x 67.08 and 70.44 (3.36 mm apart, matching), drill 0.65 x 1.7 mm; Molex edge 67.08 - 1.70 = 65.38; actual edge 64.676, so 0.704 mm extra on all 8 ports; face at 67.08 - 2.40 = 64.68, flush within 0.004 mm. The order note says the mouths are flush 'within 0.13 mm', taken from the footprint's Fab outline at x 64.545.
source: Molex SD-46765-001 rev D1 (2013-01-10), sheets 1, 2 and 5 (LCSC copy of the Molex drawing). JLC's standard routed-outline tolerance of about +/-0.2 mm is from memory, not read.
consequence: With a routed-outline tolerance of about +/-0.2 mm, the left edge can stand proud of the mouths. A thick plug overmold then may not seat fully or latch.
suggested_action: Keep the placement, and add a left-edge outline tolerance with no positive deviation in front of the eight mouths to the order note. Check that the intended cable seats and latches on the first board.

title: MC3 has no JLC stock, and stock of MC1/MC2, C5 and the 0402 100 nF capacitor covers only 39 to 76 boards.
what: JLC holds no stock of MC3, the XEM8310 mating connector, so the build depends on the recorded pre-order, whose quantity is not in the files. MC1/MC2 have 78 pieces, enough for 39 boards at two per board, and the input capacitor C5 has 76. The 0402 100 nF capacitor C0402C104K8PACTU, used 21 times per board, limits the build to about 76 boards, and Q1 to 104. Every other BOM line covers more than 180 boards.
where: HDMI Extension Board V37: MC3 QTH-040-01-F-D-DP-A (C7330812); MC1/MC2 BTE-040-01-F-D-A (C2914307); C5 EEE-FK1E221P (C128511); C0402C104K8PACTU (C2649544, 21 per board); Q1 (C141538).
evidence: jlcpcb.com/partdetail pages, 11 Nov 2026: C7330812 stock 0, presale quantity 0; C2914307 78; C128511 76; C2649544 1609 / 21 per board = 76 boards; C141538 104; C22442494 365 / 2 = 182; C22434582 230. All 66 lines of inputs/hdmi/V37_order/HDMI_Extension_Board_V37_BOM.csv were checked. C14663, C15849 and C23733 are 0 at LCSC retail but JLC holds 37.4 M, 12.4 M and 0.78 M. ORDER_NOTE_FOR_JLC_V37.md says MC3 is 'pre-ordered'.
source: JLCPCB part detail pages (jlcpcb.com/partdetail), read 11 Nov 2026.
consequence: A larger order will stall or be assembled only in part; 78 BTE connectors cover only 39 boards.
suggested_action: Confirm the MC3 pre-order quantity covers the build, and reserve MC1/MC2, C5 and C2649544 stock when the order is placed.

title: 35 parts have no LCSC number in the schematic, and the C6 BOM line names a part other than its LCSC number.
what: The order BOM gives every line an LCSC number (the JLC/LCSC stock code used to buy the part), but 35 fitted parts, mostly inherited from the BRK8310, have an empty JLCPCB field in the schematic. Their manufacturer part numbers are in the schematic, so a BOM regenerated from the design would lose only the LCSC numbers. The C6 line names TMK105BJ104KV-F, but its LCSC number C77014 is a Murata GRM155R71E104KE14D, an equivalent 100 nF 25 V X7R 0402 capacitor. C1525 also appears on two BOM lines, which is harmless but could be merged.
where: HDMI Extension Board V37 schematic and order BOM. Empty JLCPCB field: C5, C6, C7-C12, C27, C28, C31, C32, J4, Q1, R2, R7, R9-R11, R13-R15, R18, R23-R25, R28, R30-R33, U2, U4, U5, U6. HDMI_Extension_Board_V37_BOM.csv lines 'TMK105BJ104KV-F,C6,C77014', '100n,C506,C1525' and 'CL05B104KO5NNNC...,C745-C760,C1525'.
evidence: exports/hdmi/parts.csv has 270 fitted, in-BOM parts; inputs/hdmi/V37_order/HDMI_Extension_Board_V37_BOM.csv has the same 270 designators. The JLCPCB field is empty for exactly the 35 refs listed; it is present on the other 235 symbols and matches the BOM for every one (netlist.xml has no separate LCSC field). JLC part record and lcsc.com/product-detail/C77014.html (11 Nov 2026): GRM155R71E104KE14D, Murata, 0402, 100 nF, 25 V. Spot checks of 13 other numbers (C2649544, C844915, C482093, C844510, C481918, C190119, C141538, C33196, C2677392, C1511768, C22434582, C1525, C16772) all match the comment MPN; C2677392 is the DCKR reel version of SN74AXC1T45DCK.
source: Engineering judgement (BOM traceability); LCSC product page C77014 (https://www.lcsc.com/product-detail/C77014.html, read 11 Nov 2026).
consequence: JLC may query the C6 line and hold the order. A BOM exported from the project later would drop 35 LCSC numbers, so those parts would have to be sourced again from their manufacturer part numbers, with a risk of a wrong or missing part.
suggested_action: Change the C6 comment to GRM155R71E104KE14D (or mark it as a substitute), and copy the 35 LCSC numbers into the schematic JLCPCB fields at the next schematic edit.

title: U700 has thinner heat-spreading copper than TI recommends, and no thermal check exists for its high-case load.
what: The 5 V module U700 sheds its heat through 12 small vias into 15 um inner planes and small top-side ground areas; TI recommends 2 oz (about 70 um) outer copper and no less than 1 oz, and this board has 35 um outer copper. The L6 pour under it is split into six pieces, and only a 14.4 mm2 piece holds the 12 PGND vias. At the high-case load of 8 x 0.55 A it loses about 1.6 W, and with TI's reference thermal resistance the junction reaches about 93-103 C at 40-50 C ambient, 20-30 C below the 125 C limit. It gets close to 125 C only if all eight ports sit near their current limit together, which is a fault case. No thermal simulation or measurement exists.
where: HDMI Extension Board V37: U700 TPSM63606 at (124.0, 60.0), top side, 1 MHz set by R702 = 13k; PGND pads 17-20 with 12 vias of 0.3 mm drill / 0.5 mm pad; L1 zones 'U700 PGND centre / input east / output east'; L6 zone 'U700 thermal L6'.
evidence: exports/hdmi/stackup.txt: F.Cu/B.Cu 0.035 mm, In1-In4 0.0152 mm. exports/hdmi/board.json: exactly 12 DGND vias of 0.3/0.5 mm inside the PGND pad area (x 122.8-125.2, y 57.8-62.2). Fill-polygon check: L6 'U700 thermal L6' pieces 352.1, 96.7, 42.2, 19.6, 14.4 (all 12 PGND vias) and 3.9 mm2; L1 PGND centre 35.6, input east 15.3, output east 15.1 mm2. TI SLVSGB4B: efficiency 93.2% at 12 V to 5 V, 5 A, 1 MHz (p.9), so 22 W out x (1/0.932 - 1) = 1.6 W loss; RthJA 33.1 C/W on a 75 x 75 mm four-layer 2 oz board and 22.6 C/W on the EVM, psi-JT 1 C/W (p.6, section 7.4); rise about 53 C. Recommended operating TJ max 125 C; thermal shutdown 168 C typical. This board is 167.65 x 114.1 mm with six layers.
source: TI TPSM63606 datasheet SLVSGB4B (April 2022): section 7.4 p.6, efficiency p.9, layout section 11.1 p.31-32, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tpsm63606.pdf
consequence: Normal and high-case use should stay below 125 C. With all eight ports held near their current limit in a warm enclosure, the module may thermally limit and drop all eight ports at once.
suggested_action: Keep the recorded accept-and-measure handling: at bring-up, load all eight ports to the measured worst case in the intended enclosure and log the U700 case temperature (psi-JT is 1 C/W, so case is nearly junction); add airflow or a heat sink if it passes about 100 C.

title: Only two of the four XEM8310 standoff holes exist, so two module corners are held only by the connectors.
what: Opal Kelly's mating drawing for the XEM8310 calls for four 3.20 mm holes for standoffs and M3 screws, one near each corner of the 100 x 70 mm module. V37 has only MH3 and MH2, on one diagonal. Tracks on L1, L3 and L6 pass within 3.25 mm of the other two sites, so those holes cannot be added without rerouting. The two free corners are held only by the Samtec board-to-board connectors; this is a trade-off already recorded at V36.
where: HDMI Extension Board V37. Present: MH3 (147.826, 69.154) and MH2 (223.326, 131.154). Missing: (223.326, 69.154) and (147.826, 131.154). Module connectors MC1, MC2, MC3.
evidence: XEM8310-Mating-Board-Diagram-1.pdf: '4X 3.20 For standoff + mating screw (M3.0 recommended)' at x 9.00/84.50, y 4.00/66.00, outline 100.00 x 70.00. These map to the four board sites above; alignment pins match the MC1/MC2/MC3 pegs within about 0.03 mm. exports/hdmi/board.json: only MH2 and MH3 are 3.2 mm NPTH, plus a 3.5 mm centre hole at (164.676, 100.054). Tracks within 3.25 mm: B86/B87 pairs on L1/L3/L6 at (223.326, 69.154); MGT TX and B64 nets on L3/L6 at (147.826, 131.154). BRK8310_Replica_V4.kicad_pcb has all four (BRK_MH1-MH4, 3.2 mm drill, 6.5 mm pad).
source: Opal Kelly XEM8310 Mating Board Diagram, https://docs.opalkelly.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/XEM8310-Mating-Board-Diagram-1.pdf; Opal Kelly BRK8310 reference layout.
consequence: Pressing on the module, plugging in its USB-C, or vibration loads the connector solder joints at the unsupported corners, which can crack over time.
suggested_action: Record the trade-off as accepted, or add soft support under the two free corners (a glued nylon spacer or a bumper). No board change.

title: U700 reaches its 125 C junction limit at about 5.3-5.65 A in 50 C air, inside the 5.0-5.7 A high-load cases.
what: U700 is the 12 V to 5 V power module that feeds all eight ports. TI's thermal curves come from a test board with 2 oz copper on all layers; this board has thinner copper and little copper near U700 on the outer layers, so the estimated junction-to-air thermal resistance (RthJA, degrees of silicon temperature rise per watt lost) is about 33 C/W instead of 22.6 C/W. With that estimate the silicon junction reaches its 125 C rating at about 5.3-5.65 A in 50 C air and 5.6-5.95 A in 40 C air. The project's own high case (8 x 0.55 A = 4.4 A) stays at about 97-104 C in 50 C air, but the 0.63-0.71 A per-port cases from another reviewer's load finding (5.0-5.7 A total) reach 110-138 C; none of this is measured.
where: HDMI Extension Board V37, U700 TPSM63606RDLR at (124.0, 60.0), top side, set for 12 V to 5.02 V at 1 MHz by R702 13k (RT) and R700/R701 40.2k/10k (FB); net FE_5V feeding U701-U708; PGND pads 17-20 with 12 vias; L1 PGND zones 'U700 PGND centre/input east/output east'; L6 zone 'U700 thermal L6'.
evidence: SLVSGB4B p.12, 5 V / 1 MHz curves: loss 1.41 W at 4.4 A (94.0 %), about 1.8 W at 5.0 A, about 2.3 W at 5.7 A, about 2.67 W at 6.17 A (extrapolated); the earlier 1.6 W at 4.4 A (93.2 % assumed, findings/_raw/hdmi-power.json) was an overestimate. Fig. 7-13, 0 LFM: allowed air temperature about 93 C at 4.4 A, 83 C at 5 A, 70-71 C at 5.7 A, consistent with the EVM RthJA of 22.6 C/W (p.6). EVM: 2 oz on all layers (SLVUC93 p.19). This board (exports/hdmi/stackup.txt): outer 0.035 mm, inner 0.0152 mm. zones.csv: L1 U700 PGND 35.6/15.3/15.1 mm2; L6 'U700 thermal L6' 529 mm2 in 6 pieces. A 6-layer spreading model calibrated to 22.6 C/W on the EVM gives RthJA about 33 C/W (30-38) here (a review working file (not published); not re-run by the checker), matching TI's 33.1 C/W for a 4-layer 2 oz test board. TJ = TA + RthJA x P: at 50 C, 50 + 33 x 1.81 = 110 C to 50 + 38 x 1.81 = 119 C at 5.0 A; 127-139 C at 5.7 A; allowed loss at 50 C is 1.97-2.27 W, about 5.3-5.65 A.
source: TI SLVSGB4B rev. B (April 2022): section 7.3 IOUT 6 A, TJ 125 C and derating note (p.6); 7.4 RthJA 22.6 / 33.1 C/W, psiJT 1, psiJB 12.3 (p.6); TSHD 158 C minimum (p.9); Fig. 7-9, 7-10, 7-13 (p.12); 11.1 layout (outer layers preferably 2 oz, at least 1 oz). https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tpsm63606.pdf. TI SLVUC93 (Sept 2021) p.6 (200 LFM recommended above 4 A at above 1 MHz) and p.19 (2 oz on all layers), https://www.ti.com/lit/ug/slvuc93/slvuc93.pdf.
consequence: At 0.27-0.55 A per port nothing happens. If the Frontends draw 0.63-0.71 A each in 40-50 C box air, U700 runs at or above its 125 C rating with reduced life margin, and it will not shut down before 158 C; eight ports held in current limit (about 6.17 A) also exceed the 6 A output rating.
suggested_action: Set the FE_5V continuous budget at about 5.0 A (0.62 A per port) for 50 C air and check it against a measured Frontend current. At bring-up, measure U700's top temperature at 5 A in the closed box (junction is about 1 C/W above the top); if more current is needed, use 2 oz outer copper, airflow or a top-side heat sink.

title: The J4 barrel jack feeds the 7.5-15 V XEM8310 with no fuse, reverse-polarity or over-voltage protection.
what: J4 connects straight to +VDCIN, which feeds the XEM8310 module through MC2 and also feeds the 5 V module U700. J4 accepts any common 5.5/2.1 mm plug, so a 19-24 V laptop adapter or a centre-negative adapter goes directly into the XEM8310, which is specified for 7.5-15 V. The XEM8310's own barrel jack is on the same net, so plugging in both puts two adapters in parallel. This arrangement is copied from the Opal Kelly BRK8310 breakout, which has the same exposure; only the silkscreen marks the required supply.
where: HDMI Extension Board V37: J4 pin 1 at (109.08, 59.65) on +VDCIN; +VDCIN also reaches MC2.1-4, U700.1/14/16, C5 (EEE-FK1E221P, 25 V polarised aluminium), C6, C700-C703, TP710 and J920.5. Silkscreen '12 V 5 A MAX' at (97.0, 51.7) and '12V IN' at (116.75, 55.575), F.SilkS.
evidence: exports/hdmi/netlist.xml: +VDCIN has 16 nodes (C5.1, C6.2, C700-C703.1, J4.1, J920.5, MC2.1-4, TP710.1, U700.1/14/16) and none is a fuse, diode, TVS or blocking FET. exports/hdmi/pads.csv: J4.1 on +VDCIN at (109.08, 59.65). Netlist fields: J4 = PJ-063AH, 2.0 mm pin, 8 A, 24 V; C5 = EEE-FK1E221P, 25 V polarised. Opal Kelly: XEM8310 input 7.5-15 V, its own PJ-102AH centre pin on +VDCIN, no reverse or over-voltage protection mentioned. BRK8310 KiCad import (BRK8310_V1.kicad_sch): J4 PJ-102AH and C5 EEE-FK1E221P directly on VDCIN with no protection parts.
source: Opal Kelly, Powering the XEM8310, https://docs.opalkelly.com/xem8310/powering-the-xem8310/; Same Sky PJ-063AH datasheet (2.0 mm pin, 24 Vdc, 8 A), https://www.sameskydevices.com/product/resource/pj-063ah.pdf; engineering judgement.
consequence: A wrong adapter can destroy the XEM8310 module, and reversed polarity also reverse-biases C5. Two adapters in parallel back-feed each other.
suggested_action: For this order, use one labelled 12 V centre-positive adapter and keep the recorded 'never use both jacks' rule; consider a fuse, a 15-16 V TVS and a reverse-blocking FET at J4 in the next revision.

title: The J920 test-hole row puts unfused 12 V beside ground and mismatched XEM8310 rails 0.71 mm apart.
what: The nine voltage test holes sit in one row of 2.54 mm pads on a 3.25 mm pitch, leaving only 0.71 mm of bare gap, so a slipping probe can bridge two neighbours. Unfused +VDCIN (12 V) sits between two ground holes. The DDR4 1.2 V hole sits next to VIO1, which can be set up to 1.8 V; VIO1 (default 1.0 V) sits next to +1.8V; +3.3V sits next to VIO3 (default 1.2 V); and VIO3 sits next to VIO2, each settable from 1.2 to 3.3 V.
evidence: exports/hdmi/pads.csv J920 rows: pads 2.54 x 2.54 mm, drill 1.651 mm, pitch 3.25 mm, so gap 3.25 - 2.54 = 0.71 mm. exports/hdmi/netlist.xml: +1.2V_DDR = J920.1, MC3.80, R2; VIO1 = MC1.1, J920.2; +1.8V = MC1.2, J920.3; VIO3 = MC2.69, J920.8; VIO2 = MC1.80, J920.9. Opal Kelly Device Settings: VIO1 0 / 1.0 (default) / 1.2 / 1.5 / 1.8 V; VIO2 and VIO3 0 / 1.2 (default) / 1.5 / 1.8 / 2.5 / 3.3 V. The BRK8310 uses separate test points (TP1-TP8, TP17-TP19) rather than one strip. The V35 and V36 records cover only J920 plane clearance, not probe slips.
source: Engineering judgement; Opal Kelly XEM8310 Device Settings, https://docs.opalkelly.com/xem8310/device-settings/
consequence: A probe slip can short the 12 V adapter to ground or force a higher rail onto a lower XEM8310 rail, which can damage the DDR4 memory or the VIO regulators on the module.
suggested_action: Probe only with sprung hook clips or with the board unpowered; in a later revision put a ground hole between rails or space the holes further apart.

title: The back silkscreen says the red LEDs D701-D708 mean 'port 5 V on', but they light only when a port switch reports a fault.
what: The back legend reads 'D701-D708 red LED = port 5 V on', and the front table says pin 19 is 'switched per port, LED on back'. Each LED runs from FE_5V through a 3.3 kohm resistor into the FAULT pin of its TPS2553 port switch. FAULT is an open-drain output (it can only pull low) that goes low only during over-current, over-temperature or reverse voltage. So a correctly powered port has a dark LED, and a lit LED means the port is in current limit or shut down. The schematic's own note calls these 'FAULT lights', so the silkscreen contradicts the design.
where: HDMI Extension Board V37. B.SilkS text 'D701-D708 red LED = port 5 V on' at (172.00, 115.10), 1.0 mm high. F.SilkS 'switched per port, LED on back' at (107.50, 104.70). D701-D708 (bottom side) with R721-R728 (3.3k) and U701-U708 pin 4. Example: D701 at (108.20, 143.10), cathode pad at (108.20, 143.89).
evidence: exports/hdmi/netlist.xml, for n = 1..8: Net-(D70n-K) = D70n.1 (K) and U70n.4 FAULT only; Net-(D70n-A) = D70n.2 (A) and R72n.1; R72n.2 = FE_5V. The board text dump (pcbnew, a review working file (not published)) contains the two legend strings above. The schematic note for U701-U708 says the red LEDs indicate each switch FAULT, and that R721-R728 / D701-D708 were added as FAULT lights. TI SLVS841G Table 5-1 p.4: FAULT is an active-low open-drain output, asserted during overcurrent, overtemperature or reverse-voltage. The earlier review confirmed that regenerated order Gerbers are byte-identical to the board, so the legend will be printed as drawn. The enclosure V3 record lists service windows for the dial, SW601, headers and J920, but none for these bottom-side LEDs.
source: TI TPS2553 datasheet SLVS841G (revised Oct 2026), Table 5-1 Pin Functions, p.4, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps2553.pdf; boards/hdmi/HDMI_Extension_Board_V37.kicad_sch (U701-U708 function note); boards/hdmi/HDMI_Extension_Board_V37.kicad_pcb; inputs/hdmi/enclosure_V3/START_HERE.md 'Outside' table.
consequence: At bring-up, a healthy board shows eight dark LEDs, which the legend says means every port is off. A port stuck in current limit (the HDMI-01 risk) lights its LED, which the legend says means 'on'. The most likely port failure would read as success, and debugging would start on the wrong board.
suggested_action: Silkscreen-only change: make the back legend 'D701-D708 red = port FAULT (over-current / over-temperature); off = normal' and the front text 'FAULT LED on back'. Then regenerate the silkscreen Gerbers if this is done before ordering.

title: The board does not show which setting the JTAG selectors SW600 and SW601 are in, so the target port and the OFF position cannot be read from the board.
what: SW600 is a 9-position rotary switch with a plain flatted shaft. The silkscreen says 'JTAG TARGET: 0 = XEM, 1-8 = P1-P8', but there is no dial, index or position number around the shaft: only two outline lines and a pin-1 corner mark. Alps lists 40-degree steps and no index marking, and its catalog numbers the positions 1-9, not 0-8. SW601 is a slide switch whose slider moves along the board's y axis. Its label 'OFF/ENABLE' is a single line below the switch with no arrow, so nothing shows which end is OFF.
where: HDMI Extension Board V37. SW600 (ALPS SRBQ490100) at (196.0, 56.5): terminals 1, 2, 4-10 = SEL_0..SEL_8 (XEM, P1..P8), common = terminal 3; legend at (196.15, 63.83). SW601 (JS202011JCQN) at (184.6, 55.0), rotated 90 degrees, pads at x 183.4/185.8 and y 52.5/55.0/57.5; legend 'OFF/ENABLE' box x 179.21-188.79, y 60.55-62.25.
evidence: pcbnew dump (a review working file (not published)). SW600 silk is two lines at y 49.77-49.92 and 62.67-62.83 plus a corner mark at x 202.53-203.47, y 49.83-50.77; there is no other silk or text inside the switch area. SW601 silk is an outline only. Netlist: SW601 pin 2 ROTARY_COMMON goes to pin 1 DGND or pin 3 (open); pin 6 MASTER goes to pin 5 +3.3V or pin 7 DGND. The 'enable' throws (pins 1/5) are at y 57.5 and the 'off' throws (pins 3/7) at y 52.5. Which slider end connects which throws depends on the C&K contact layout, which could not be read. Alps catalog product list: SRBQ490100, 1 pole, 9 positions, 40 +/-3 degrees, flat actuator. The Alps product page lists no index or stop.
source: Alps Alpine SRBQ series catalog p.1 product list, https://tech.alpsalpine.com/cms.media/product_catalog_sw_04_srbq_en_aaa09fb719.pdf; Alps product page, https://tech.alpsalpine.com/e/products/detail/SRBQ490100/; C&K JS series datasheet not readable (littelfuse.com access denied); engineering judgement.
consequence: All eight Frontends carry the same XC7A35T, so Vivado cannot tell which port it is connected to; a bitstream or flash image can go to the wrong head. The HDMI-05 workaround ('keep SW601 OFF until the EEPROM is programmed') cannot be followed from the board alone.
suggested_action: Add silkscreen ticks numbered 0-8 at the SW600 detent angles (or fit a knob with a pointer). Print 'OFF' and 'ENABLE' at the two ends of SW601's travel, after confirming the direction with a meter on the first board (MASTER to +3.3V means ENABLE).

title: Enclosure V3 powers the DFR1169 and the XEM8310 from the same 12 V with the Thunderbolt cable left in, so the endpoint can miss first link training, and nothing documents whether the Mac finds it later.
what: In enclosure V3 the adapter takes its 12 V from TP710/TP709, so switching on J4 starts the adapter, its Thunderbolt link to the Mac and the XEM boot together. With a standard build the endpoint cannot be counted on at first link training. An adapter that follows PCIe card timing releases PERST# about 100 ms after slot power and expects training within 20 ms, but the XEM needs 0.26-0.49 s plus its rail ramp; being present needs a Tandem PROM build, a fixed order (board first, then Thunderbolt) or a re-plug after boot. The board side is sound, because U4 holds E22 in reset until the adapter powers the slot and releases PERST#, but no DFRobot document says whether the adapter retries the link or whether macOS enumerates a late endpoint, and no public JHL6340 datasheet exists.
where: Enclosure V3 adapter feed: TP710 (+VDCIN, 117.0/58.0) and TP709 (DGND, 133.5/57.0). PERST# path: J6.A11 -> TP14 (116.25/142.33) -> U4 SN74AXC1T45, B to A (DIR = DGND; VCCB = +3.3V_PCIE_C from J6.A9/A10/B8; VCCA = +1.2V_DDR via R2 0 ohm) -> TP13 (116.00/136.13) -> R7 0 ohm -> MC3.78 -> E22. XEM user LEDs D1-D4 on bank 65.
evidence: inputs/hdmi/enclosure_V3/START_HERE.md line 39 (one USB-C to the computer), line 49 (adapter lead from TP710 and TP709), line 64 (enumeration on the lab's Mac untested). exports/hdmi/netlist.xml: /PCIE_PERST_B_3V3 = J6.A11, TP14, U4.4; U4.5 DIR = DGND; U4.6 = +3.3V_PCIE_C (J6.A9/A10/B8, C12); U4.1 via R2 from +1.2V_DDR (MC3.80); /PCIE_PERST_B_VIO = U4.3, TP13, R7.1; R7.2 = B67_T3U_N12 = MC3.78; no other part on these nets. TI SCES882E: DIR low = B to A; both ports high-Z if VCCA or VCCB is below 100 mV; 288 kOhm static pull-down on every data I/O (7.3.2), so E22 reads reset until slot 3.3 V exists. DFR1169 wiki: lists power inputs, the JHL6340, PCIe 3.0 x4 and the LEDs, but gives no slot-power timing, PERST#, hot-plug or rescan data. Its drawing has only dimensions and slot pin labels. Its tutorial powers the dock first, connects the Thunderbolt cable last, and says only that the dock supports hot swapping. A part-number search found no public JHL6340 datasheet. Boot time is from the previous finding. That a PCIe downstream port keeps retrying link detection is from memory, not re-read.
source: DFRobot DFR1169 wiki, https://wiki.dfrobot.com/DFR1169 ; DFRobot tutorial 'Example for LattePanda - Connecting Thunderbolt Docking Station', https://wiki.dfrobot.com/dfr1169/docs/18973 ; DFR1169 dimension drawing V1.0, https://dfimg.dfrobot.com/wiki/18624/DFR1169_thunderbolt-to-pcie-module_dimension_V1.0.pdf ; TI SN74AXC1T45 SCES882E (Dec 2023): features, DIR pin table, sections 7.3.2 and 7.3.4, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/sn74axc1t45.pdf ; AMD PG213 v1.3 'Tandem Configuration' (100 ms / 20 ms), https://docs.amd.com/r/en-US/pg213-pcie4-ultrascale-plus/Tandem-Configuration ; Opal Kelly 'PCI Express Reference Design', Standard Configuration power-on procedure, https://docs.opalkelly.com/xem8310/brk8310-breakout-board/pci-express-reference-design/ ; Opal Kelly XEM8310 'LEDs', https://docs.opalkelly.com/xem8310/leds/ ; Intel JHL6340 product listing (part-number search only; no datasheet found), https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/products/sku/94032/intel-jhl6340-thunderbolt-3-controller/specifications.html ; inputs/hdmi/enclosure_V3/START_HERE.md; exports/hdmi/netlist.xml and pads.csv.
consequence: In normal use of the box (cable left in, 12 V switched on), the Mac may show no XEM8310 PCIe device, sometimes or every time. It will look like an adapter, cable or driver fault and cost bring-up time.
suggested_action: Bring-up notes: unplug the Thunderbolt cable, switch on 12 V, wait at least 1 s (an XEM user LED driven by the PCIe core's link-up helps), then plug the cable in, and re-plug it after any XEM reconfiguration. Once, with the cable left in, scope TP14 and TP13 against TP710, and record whether the Mac lists the endpoint (vendor 0x10EE, from memory) with and without a re-plug.

title: With SW601 at ENABLE and SW600 at 0, a connected Vivado Hardware Manager reaches the XEM JTAG 12-28 ms after power-up and can break its 0.26-0.49 s boot from flash.
what: Opal Kelly warns that an active JTAG connection disturbs the XEM8310's power-on load from flash, and asks for JTAG adapters to be removed before testing it. AMD UG908 says Hardware Manager polling can interrupt a Master SPI load and cause intermittent power-up failures. On this board the adapter is built in: U610 joins the XEM JTAG pins to the shared trunk whenever SW600 is at 0 and SW601 at ENABLE, and U602 starts driving the trunk 12-28 ms after the XEM's 3.3 V and 1.8 V outputs come up, long before the boot ends. Of all switch, USB and software states, only SW601 ENABLE + SW600 0 + USB-C plugged + a JTAG tool scanning is active; the same rule covers the Frontend selected at positions 1-8, and the silk does not show which SW601 end is OFF.
where: MC2.71/72/74/76 (JTAG_TDO/TMS/TDI/TCK) -> U610 TS3A27518E (EN = SEL_0) -> JTAG_*_1V8 trunk -> U602 TXU0304 -> U501 FT232H. U602 OE = DRIVE_ENABLE from U605 TPS3808G30 (CT open), whose MR comes from U603 TPS3700 and R614 to MASTER. U602 VCCA = FTDI3V3 from USB-C J500; VCCB = +1.8V from MC1.2. SW600 (silk 'JTAG TARGET: 0 = XEM, 1-8 = P1-P8' at 196.15/63.83); SW601 (silk 'OFF/ENABLE' at 184.0/61.4); R620-R628; MASTER probe at R600.1 (187.6, 57.775), top side.
evidence: exports/hdmi/netlist.xml: MC2.71/72/74/76 -> U610 NO5/NO3/NO6/NO4; COM5/3/6/4 -> JTAG_TDO/TMS/TDI/TCK_1V8 (R601-R603 22 ohm) -> U602 B side and U611-U618 COM. U610 pin 20 = SEL_0 (R620 10k to +3.3V = MC2.70); grounded only via SW600.1 -> ROTARY_COMMON -> SW601 pads 2-1. U610 IN1/IN2 = +3.3V. TI SCDS260F Table 8-1: EN high = all off; EN low with IN high = COM to NO. U602.8 = DRIVE_ENABLE = U605.1 (R615 12k up, R616 100k down); U605 SENSE/VDD = +3.3V; CT (pin 4) unconnected; MR = WINDOW_GATE = U603 OUTA/OUTB + R614 4.7k to MASTER. MASTER = SW601 pad 6: +3.3V in ENABLE, DGND in OFF; R600 3.3k to DGND. VREF_SELECTED comes from +1.8V via R629 1k when U610 is on. TI SBVS050N: tD 12/20/28 ms with CT open. U602.1 = FTDI3V3 = U501.39, fed only from J500 VBUS via FB502. TI SCES935A: U602 outputs high-Z when OE is low or either VCC is below 100 mV. State table (SW601 / SW600 / USB-C / JTAG tool -> XEM TAP during boot): OFF / any / any / any: isolated, not active. ENABLE / 1-8 / any / any: U610 off, XEM isolated, not active (the selected Frontend is exposed instead). ENABLE / 0 / USB out: U602 unpowered and high-Z, not active. ENABLE / 0 / USB in / no tool scanning: static FT232H idle levels, not active. ENABLE / 0 / USB in / Vivado Hardware Manager connected (EEPROM written by program_ftdi) or another tool scanning: ACTIVE. Exposure: U602 is on 12-28 ms after the XEM rails; boot ends 263-492 ms after the FPGA rails. SW601's footprint silk is only an outline; its slider travels along y and the single 'OFF/ENABLE' string marks no end.
source: Opal Kelly XEM8310 'Flash Memory', section 'Loading a Power-On FPGA Configuration', https://docs.opalkelly.com/xem8310/flash-memory/ ; AMD UG908 2026.1 (23 Jun 2026), 'Configuration Failures in Master Mode', https://docs.amd.com/r/en-US/ug908-vivado-programming-debugging/Configuration-Failures-in-Master-Mode ; UG908 'Programming FTDI Devices for Vivado Hardware Manager Support', https://docs.amd.com/r/en-US/ug908-vivado-programming-debugging/Programming-FTDI-Devices-for-Vivado-Hardware-Manager-Support ; TI TS3A27518E SCDS260F (Dec 2021), section 8.4 Table 8-1, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ts3a27518e.pdf ; TI TXU0304 SCES935A (Nov 2021), features p.1 and sections 9.3.1.1 and 9.3.5, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/txu0304.pdf ; TI TPS3808 SBVS050N (Aug 2026), tD table and section 7.3.2, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps3808.pdf ; exports/hdmi/netlist.xml, pads.csv, parts.csv; boards/hdmi/HDMI_Extension_Board_V37.kicad_pcb (gr_text at lines 86569 and 86580; SW601 footprint graphics).
consequence: While someone debugs the PCIe endpoint with Vivado open, power cycles will sometimes leave the XEM unconfigured: no endpoint, and no port clocks or commands. That is easy to mistake for an adapter or enumeration fault.
suggested_action: Bring-up notes: power up with SW601 at OFF every time (check that MASTER at R600.1 reads 0 V), and use SW601 ENABLE with SW600 at 0 only to program or debug the XEM. Before power-cycling with Vivado open, close the Hardware Manager or run set_param xicom.allow_cfgin_commands false (UG908).

title: A full XCAU25P bitstream takes 0.26-0.49 s to load from the XEM8310 flash, 2.6-4.9 times the PCIe 100 ms boot limit, so only a Tandem PROM build can meet it.
what: PCIe lets PERST# (the slot reset) be released about 100 ms after power is good. The endpoint must then be ready to train its link within 20 ms, and Opal Kelly says the XEM8310 must be available when the host enumerates. At power-up the XEM8310 loads its whole 123.4 Mb XCAU25P bitstream from quad-SPI flash. At Opal Kelly's 85 MHz flash rate, with the internal clock's +/-15 % tolerance and up to 65 ms of power-on reset, that ends 0.32-0.49 s after the FPGA rails are up (0.26-0.42 s at the 102 MHz rate in Opal Kelly's Tandem example). Tandem PROM, which AMD supports on the XCAU25P, loads a small first stage that brings up the PCIe block first; a standard build works only if the XEM is configured before the host looks.
where: XEM8310 FPGA (XCAU25P; Opal Kelly reference xcau25p-ffvb676-2-e) and its IS25WP256D flash on bank 0. PCIe x4 on quad 225 (MC3 21-36); refclk T7/T6 (MC3.17/19 via C7/C8 from J6.A13/A14); pcie_reset_n E22 (MC3.78 via R7 and U4). inputs/hdmi/firmware_V34/fit_pins_V34.xdc lines 60-62.
evidence: UG570 Table 1: AU25P = 123,449,056 bits (41,476 frames x 93 words). DS931 v1.9 configuration switching table: TPOR 0-65 ms with POR_OVERRIDE low (5-15 ms with override and a 2 ms ramp), counted from the last of VCCINT/VCCBRAM/VCCAUX/VCCO_0 at 95 %; FMCCKTOL +/-15 %. Load time = 123,449,056 / (4 x CCLK). CONFIGRATE 85: CCLK 72.25 / 85 / 97.75 MHz gives 427.2 / 363.1 / 315.7 ms; with TPOR, 316-492 ms. CONFIGRATE 102: 356.0 / 302.6 / 263.1 ms; with TPOR, 263-421 ms. Ratio: 2.6-4.9 times 100 ms, 2.2-4.1 times 120 ms (100 + 20). PG213 Supported Devices: AU25P PCIE40E4_X0Y0, Tandem Production. PG213 PROM Selection: the Tandem PROM file is 4-5 % larger, about 129.6 Mb, inside the 256 Mb flash. Stage-1 budget at the minimum 289 Mb/s with 65 ms TPOR: at most 10.1 Mb for 100 ms, or 15.9 Mb for 120 ms; PG213's own VU9P example stage 1 is 11.8 Mb. PG213 'Moving the PCIe Reset Pins': a reset pin outside bank 65 enlarges stage 1; here it is E22 in bank 67, as in Opal Kelly's example. Opal Kelly known issue: Tandem breaks the IP example design in Vivado 2023.1/2023.2. Opal Kelly publishes no module rail-ramp or POR_OVERRIDE data. Calculation: W2/a review working file (not published), output config_time.txt.
source: AMD UG570 (release 4 Mar 2025), 'Device Resources and Configuration Bitstream Lengths' Table 1, https://docs.amd.com/r/en-US/ug570-ultrascale-configuration/Device-Resources-and-Configuration-Bitstream-Lengths ; UG570 'POR_OVERRIDE', https://docs.amd.com/r/en-US/ug570-ultrascale-configuration/POR_OVERRIDE ; AMD DS931 v1.9 (19 May 2026), 'Configuration Switching Characteristics' (TPOR, FMCCKTOL, FMCCK_START), https://docs.amd.com/r/en-US/ds931-artix-ultrascale-plus/Configuration-Switching-Characteristics ; AMD PG213 v1.3 (31 Jul 2026), 'Tandem Configuration', https://docs.amd.com/r/en-US/pg213-pcie4-ultrascale-plus/Tandem-Configuration , 'Supported Devices', https://docs.amd.com/r/en-US/pg213-pcie4-ultrascale-plus/Supported-Devices , 'PROM Selection', https://docs.amd.com/r/en-US/pg213-pcie4-ultrascale-plus/PROM-Selection , 'Calculating Bitstream Load Time for Tandem', https://docs.amd.com/r/en-US/pg213-pcie4-ultrascale-plus/Calculating-Bitstream-Load-Time-for-Tandem , 'Moving the PCIe Reset Pins', https://docs.amd.com/r/en-US/pg213-pcie4-ultrascale-plus/Moving-the-PCIe-Reset-Pins ; Opal Kelly 'PCI Express Reference Design' (BRK8310), Standard and Tandem Configuration sections and Known Issues, https://docs.opalkelly.com/xem8310/brk8310-breakout-board/pci-express-reference-design/ ; Opal Kelly 'Flash Memory', https://docs.opalkelly.com/xem8310/flash-memory/ ; Opal Kelly 'Powering the XEM8310' (no timing given), https://docs.opalkelly.com/xem8310/powering-the-xem8310/ ; inputs/hdmi/firmware_V34/fit_pins_V34.xdc.
consequence: With a standard build, the endpoint exists only about 0.3-0.5 s after power, plus the module's rail ramp. A host or adapter that trains and enumerates on PCIe timing finds nothing. The PCIe link, the only host path that can carry eight stacks (SYS-12), is then missing until a re-plug or reboot.
suggested_action: Decide the XEM boot method before writing its firmware. Either use a Tandem PROM build whose write_bitstream log shows a stage 1 of at most about 10 Mb (16 Mb under the 120 ms reading), or use a standard build plus the fixed power-up order in the next finding.

title: The XEM8310 constraint files set none of Opal Kelly's flash-boot options, so a default build would take about 46 s to load from flash.
what: Opal Kelly lists five settings for a bitfile that boots from the XEM8310 flash: quad-SPI mode and bus width, falling-edge capture, an 85 MHz configuration clock and the internal clock source. The project's three XEM constraint files contain none of them, and no Vivado build has been run. With Vivado's UltraScale+ defaults (x1 bus at 2.7 MHz), the 123.4 Mb file would take about 46 s to load, which defeats any power-up order. Opal Kelly also notes that a bitfile built with these settings cannot be loaded through FrontPanel download, so the flow needs a separate flash build.
where: inputs/hdmi/firmware_V34/fit_pins_V34.xdc, fit_pins_V34_sync.xdc and header_pins_V34.xdc; XEM8310 FPGA flash IS25WP256D on bank 0.
evidence: A grep of the three files for CONFIG, SPI_BUSWIDTH, CONFIGRATE, EXTMASTERCCLK, COMPRESS, SPI_FALL and BITSTREAM finds no match. inputs/hdmi/V34_record/START_HERE.md line 15 names these files as the board's XDC set; inputs/hdmi/V36_prefab_fixes/START_HERE.md line 67 says a Vivado build was never run. UG908 UltraScale+ bitstream settings: CONFIGRATE default 2.7 (85.0 and 102.0 are allowed), SPI_BUSWIDTH default NONE, EXTMASTERCCLK_EN default Disable. Load times: 123,449,056 bits / 2.7 MHz = 45.7 s (39.8-53.8 s at the DS931 +/-15 % tolerance); x4 at 2.7 MHz = 11.4 s; x1 at 85 MHz = 1.45 s. Opal Kelly's Flash Memory page lists CONFIG_MODE SPIx4, SPI_BUSWIDTH 4, SPI_FALL_EDGE YES, CONFIGRATE 85.0 and EXTMASTERCCLK_EN disable, and says these bitfiles load only into flash. UG908 lists is25wp256d as a supported Artix UltraScale+ configuration memory.
source: Opal Kelly XEM8310 'Flash Memory', section 'XDC Constraints for FPGA Flash Configuration', https://docs.opalkelly.com/xem8310/flash-memory/ ; AMD UG908 2026.1, 'Artix, Virtex, and Kintex UltraScale+ Bitstream Settings', https://docs.amd.com/r/en-US/ug908-vivado-programming-debugging/Artix-Virtex-and-Kintex-UltraScale-Bitstream-Settings ; UG908 'Artix UltraScale+ Configuration Memory Devices', https://docs.amd.com/r/en-US/ug908-vivado-programming-debugging/Artix-UltraScale-Configuration-Memory-Devices ; AMD UG570 Table 1, https://docs.amd.com/r/en-US/ug570-ultrascale-configuration/Device-Resources-and-Configuration-Bitstream-Lengths ; AMD DS931 v1.9 (FMCCKTOL), https://docs.amd.com/r/en-US/ds931-artix-ultrascale-plus/Configuration-Switching-Characteristics ; inputs/hdmi/firmware_V34/*.xdc; inputs/hdmi/V34_record/START_HERE.md; inputs/hdmi/V36_prefab_fixes/START_HERE.md.
consequence: A first XEM flash image built from the present constraints would come up tens of seconds after power. The PCIe endpoint would then miss enumeration in every power-up order except a long wait, and the delay is easy to misread as a dead board.
suggested_action: Put Opal Kelly's five flash lines (plus COMPRESS and the Tandem option, if chosen) in a separate XEM flash-build XDC, and keep the FrontPanel-download build without them.

title: Header J910 mixes 1.8 V bank-64 holes with VIO2 bank-84 holes, and the silk does not give each bank's voltage.
what: J910 puts bank 64 I/O (an HP bank, 1.90 V maximum, powered by VIO1) beside bank 84 I/O (an HD bank, up to 3.40 V, powered by VIO2), and it also brings out VIO2, VREF1, VBATT and VIO1. A jumper from VIO2 at 3.3 V to a bank 64 hole would over-drive that bank. VBATT is tied to ground on the module through a 0 ohm resistor, and on modules built with C1 fitted (PCN-10166) VREF1 has 1 kohm to ground. The back silk already names the bank of each hole but not its voltage.
where: HDMI Extension Board V37, J910: pins 1-7, 10, 20 bank 64; pins 9, 11-16, 18, 19, 21-26, 28 bank 84; 8 VREF1; 17 VIO2; 27 VBATT; 29 DGND; 30 VIO1. B.SilkS legend above J910 (y 133.62).
evidence: exports/hdmi/pads.csv J910 rows: 1 B64_L12P_GC, 2 B64_T1U_N12, 3 B64_L14P_GC, 4 B64_L12N_GC, 5 B64_T0U_N12, 6 B64_L14N_GC, 7 B64_L20P, 8 VREF1, 10 B64_T3U_N12, 20 B64_T2U_N12, 17 VIO2, 27 VBATT, 29 DGND, 30 VIO1, the rest B84_*. VREF1 = J910.8 + MC1.4 only; VBATT = J910.27 + MC1.79 only; VIO2 = J910.17, J920.9, MC1.80. inputs/hdmi/firmware_V34/header_pins_V34.xdc confirms the banks. Back silk shows bank-coded names ('1 64L12P*', '9 84L1P', '17 VIO2', '27 VBATT'). A 1.8 V jumper into VREF1 draws about 1.8 mA.
source: Opal Kelly XEM8310 Expansion Connectors, https://docs.opalkelly.com/xem8310/expansion-connectors/ ; Opal Kelly PCN-10166 (14 June 2023), https://docs.opalkelly.com/xem8310/product-lifecycle/pcn-10166/
consequence: A bench wiring error can over-drive bank 64 or short a battery or reference source to ground.
suggested_action: Add the bank voltage per row (bank 64 = VIO1 up to 1.8 V, bank 84 = VIO2) to the board's START_HERE now and to the silk legend at the next revision.

title: Frontend JTAG TMS runs on Micro-HDMI pin 2 (Utility), a wire some cables do not connect.
what: On every port, pin 2 of the Micro-HDMI (Type D) connector carries the JTAG TMS line to the Frontend. HDMI calls pin 2 the Utility (HEAC+) pin; it was reserved before HDMI 1.4 and is needed only for the Ethernet and Audio Return channel, so some cables may leave it unwired. Pin 15 (the HDMI CEC pin, here TDI) is also sometimes left out of cheap cables. If pin 2 is open, JTAG to that Frontend fails while power and data links still work; the board files cannot settle this, only a continuity test of the actual cables can.
where: HDMI Extension Board V37, J610-J617: pin 1 HDMIn_VREF, pin 2 HDMIn_JTAG_TMS (e.g. HDMI1_JTAG_TMS = J610.2, R642.2), pin 15 TDI, 17 TCK, 18 TDO, 19 PORTn_5V. Frontend FPGA Board J3.2 FPGA_JTAG_TMS.
evidence: exports/hdmi/pads.csv: the J610-J617 pin assignments above; HDMI1_JTAG_TMS on J610.2 and R642.2. exports/frontend/pads.csv: J3.2 FPGA_JTAG_TMS. Public HDMI pinout summaries state the Utility conductor (Type A pin 14, Type D pin 2) is optional for HEAC in HDMI 1.4 and later; a cable-quality application note lists a missing pin 14 among cable defects it has seen. The HDMI specification itself was not read.
source: HDMI Type D pin assignment from secondary sources (public pinout summaries and a cable-quality application note); the HDMI specification was not read. Engineering judgement.
consequence: JTAG programming and debug of a Frontend fail on any port used with a cable that lacks pin 2 (or pin 15).
suggested_action: Buy 'High Speed with Ethernet' cables and buzz pins 1, 2, 15, 17, 18 and 19 end to end on each cable type before use.

title: Port power follows only U700's power-good, so the FPGA cannot switch, reset or monitor any Frontend.
what: All eight port switches are turned on together by U700's power-good (PG) output, a signal that goes high only while the 5 V rail is inside its window. If the rail falls below about 94 % or rises above about 107 % for more than 120 us, every port turns off at once and returns about 2 ms after PG recovers. The switches' fault outputs only light red LEDs on the bottom side; no XEM pin or header can read them or drive the enable. A hung Frontend can only be power-cycled by pulling its cable or the 12 V input.
where: HDMI Extension Board V37, net PORT_ENABLE (U700.13 PG, R703 10k pull-up to FE_5V, U701-U708 pin 3 EN); FAULT U701-U708 pin 4 to D701-D708 (bottom side) via R721-R728 from FE_5V.
evidence: exports/hdmi/netlist.xml: PORT_ENABLE = R703.1, U700.13, U701-U708 pin 3 (10 nodes), no MC1/MC2/MC3 pin or header; R703.2 = FE_5V; Net-(D701-K) = D701.1 + U701.4 FAULT; Net-(D701-A) = D701.2 + R721.1, R721.2 = FE_5V. nets.csv: PORT_ENABLE 10 pads, 162 mm of track. parts.csv: D701-D708 side = bottom. TPSM63606 PG: UV falling 92/94/96.5 %, OV rising 105/107/110 %, hysteresis 1.3 %, 120 us filter, rising delay 1.5/2.0/2.5 ms (taken from TI search snippets; page numbers not re-checked).
source: TI TPSM63606 datasheet SLVSGB4B (April 2022), section 8.3.9 and the PG rows of the electrical characteristics table, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tpsm63606.pdf; engineering judgement.
consequence: Remote power-cycling and fault reporting need a cable pull, and one rail disturbance resets all eight stacks at once.
suggested_action: Accept for this order. In a later revision, route PORT_ENABLE or per-port EN and a wired-OR FAULT to spare XEM pins.

title: The +/-12 V converter's start-up surge lasts about 8 ms, not 1-2 ms, and adds about 0.1-0.25 A at the 5 V port pin while it ramps.
what: The LT3582-12 has a fixed 1 uA ramp current. With the 10 nF RAMPP/RAMPN capacitors, both outputs rise together at 1.5 V/ms and need about 8 ms to reach 12 V. Charging the 22 uF output and 10 uF LDO-input capacitors at that rate (about 10-25 uF per side after DC-bias loss) takes 15-38 mA per side at 12 V.
